unit.title: Advertising law in France
unit.description: Influencer law, retouched and AI images, price reductions, misleading practices, green claims, Loi Evin, Loi Toubon, comparative ads, AI Act labels

cards.definition: The law of 9 June 2023 treats commercial influence as advertising. Paid content must show Publicité or Collaboration commerciale clearly for the whole content; some promotions are banned (cosmetic surgery, nicotine products, among others). Penalties go up to 2 years in prison and 300,000 euros, and the brand shares liability.
cards.example: A sponsored Reel must display the mention on screen from start to end, not only in the caption.

cards.definition: Under the same law, promotional images where a face or silhouette was modified must carry the French mention for retouched images, and those generated by AI the mention for virtual images.
cards.example: A creator slims her waist with a filter in a sponsored post: the retouched image mention is mandatory.

cards.definition: Since May 2022 (article L112-1-1 of the consumer code), any announced price reduction must show as reference price the lowest price charged in the 30 days before the promotion. The EU Court of Justice ruled in 2024 that the discount must be computed from that price.
cards.example: A product sold 49 euros, raised to 69 euros a week before Black Friday, cannot be announced as minus 30 percent from 69 euros.

cards.definition: False or confusing claims, fake reviews, fake urgency, hidden costs or omissions that mislead consumers. The DGCCRF enforces; penalties can reach 2 years in prison and fines up to 10 percent of annual turnover.
cards.example: Displaying only 2 left on every product whatever the real stock.

cards.definition: Environmental claims must be precise and proven. EU directive 2024/825 applies from 27 September 2026 and bans generic claims such as eco-friendly or green without proof of recognized excellent performance; France was still finishing its transposition in autumn 2026, but misleading green claims were already sanctioned.
cards.example: Replace eco-friendly bottle with bottle made of 50 percent recycled plastic.

cards.definition: Strictly limits alcohol and tobacco advertising. Alcohol ads may only give objective information (origin, degree, composition, way of making, taste), must carry a health warning, are banned on TV and in cinemas, and are allowed online under conditions, never on services mainly aimed at young people.
cards.example: A wine ad can describe the vineyard and the grapes, not show a party where drinking makes you popular.

cards.definition: Advertising aimed at the French public must be in French. Foreign words and slogans are allowed if a French translation is just as readable and audible; registered brand names are exempt.
cards.example: An English slogan on a poster in Paris needs a French translation of the same size.

cards.definition: Allowed in France if it is not misleading, compares products meeting the same need, compares objectively one or more essential, verifiable features (price included), and does not denigrate the competitor.
cards.example: Our basket of 50 products costs 12 percent less than at Brand X, survey of 3 March, details on our site.

cards.definition: Since 2 August 2026, article 50 of the EU AI Act requires telling people they are talking to an AI (chatbots) and disclosing deepfakes, images, audio or video generated or manipulated by AI that look real.
cards.example: An ad using an AI-generated video of a realistic person must say it was made with AI.

exercises.prompt: A creator is paid to present your product in a TikTok video. What must appear?
choices: Publicité or Collaboration commerciale, clearly, during the whole video
Only the hashtag #ad at the end of the caption
Nothing, if the product is genuinely good
The price of the collaboration in euros
exercises.explain: The 2023 law requires a clear mention for the whole duration, readable on the image or video itself.

exercises.prompt: Which promotion is banned for influencers in France?
choices: Cosmetic surgery procedures
Organic food products
Second-hand clothing apps
Online language courses
exercises.explain: The law bans promoting cosmetic surgery, nicotine products and some other risky offers; many others are strictly regulated.

exercises.prompt: A sponsored photo of a face was smoothed with a filter. What does French law require?
choices: The mention for retouched images
Nothing, filters are allowed freely
Deleting the photo within 24 hours
A note in the bio of the account
exercises.explain: Modified faces or silhouettes in promotional content need the retouched image mention; AI-generated ones the virtual image mention.

exercises.prompt: Under the French influencer law, a brand can be held liable together with the creator it pays.
exercises.explain: True. The advertiser shares liability for breaches. Check content and mentions before publication.

exercises.prompt: A jacket sold 80 euros all month is marked 120 euros the week before Black Friday, then shown at minus 40 percent. What is wrong?
choices: The reference must be 80 euros, the lowest price of the last 30 days
Nothing: the shop can choose any reference price
Black Friday discounts cannot exceed 30 percent
Prices cannot change in the month before a sale
exercises.explain: Article L112-1-1: the reference price is the lowest of the 30 previous days, and the percentage is computed from it.

exercises.prompt: Which practice is a misleading commercial practice?
choices: A countdown that restarts at every visit
A dated launch offer that really ends
Showing the real stock left in the shop
Publishing all reviews, good and bad
exercises.explain: Fake urgency misleads consumers. Real deadlines and real stock information are fine.

exercises.prompt: Since September 2026, which claim is risky without detailed proof?
choices: Eco-friendly packaging
Packaging made of 70 percent recycled cardboard
Bottle weight reduced by 20 percent since 2023
Product made in our factory in Lyon
exercises.explain: Generic claims (eco-friendly, green, natural friend) are targeted by EU directive 2024/825. Precise, verifiable claims are the way.

exercises.prompt: A wine brand wants a social media ad. What does the Loi Evin allow?
choices: Objective information: origin, grapes, taste, degree
Young people partying thanks to the wine
A promise that wine helps you relax
A TV spot during the evening news
exercises.explain: Alcohol ads must stay objective and informative, carry the health warning, and never link drinking to success or social life.

exercises.prompt: A brand uses the English slogan Just feel it on posters in France. What does the Loi Toubon require?
choices: A French translation just as readable
Nothing, slogans are always exempt
Removing every English word from posters
A translation in small print at the bottom
exercises.explain: Foreign words are allowed if a French version is equally legible. Registered trademarks are exempt.

exercises.prompt: Which comparative ad is lawful in France?
choices: Our basket is 12 percent cheaper than Brand X, dated survey online
Brand X products are bad and even dangerous for you
We are better than every competitor, just trust us
Brand X is about to go bankrupt, so buy from us
exercises.explain: Comparisons must be objective, verifiable and fair. Denigration and unproven claims are not allowed.

exercises.prompt: Since August 2026, a realistic AI-generated video used in an ad must be disclosed as AI-generated.
exercises.explain: True. Article 50 of the AI Act requires disclosing deepfakes and telling users when they talk to an AI system.

exercises.title: Black Friday for an online shop
exercises.scenario: Your fashion shop plans Black Friday: minus 50 percent banners, influencer posts, an AI-generated model in the ads and the slogan Shop green this Friday.

steps.prompt: Some products were 39 euros all October and now show 79 euros crossed out. What do you do?
choices: Use 39 euros as reference and recompute the discount
Keep 79 euros: it is the official list price
Remove the old price and show only the new one
Raise prices a month earlier to be safe
steps.feedback: The reference is the lowest price of the last 30 days. Inflating it beforehand is exactly what the rule targets.

steps.prompt: The influencers retouch their silhouette in the photos. What must the posts include?
choices: The commercial mention and the retouched image mention
Only a #sponsored tag at the end of the caption
Nothing, if the shop did not ask for the retouching
A link to the general terms of the shop
steps.feedback: Both mentions are required, and the brand shares liability for the content it pays for.

steps.prompt: Marketing wants to keep Shop green this Friday. What do you advise?
choices: Drop it or replace it with a precise, proven claim
Keep it: it is only a play on words
Add a small leaf logo to make it credible
Use it only in the influencer posts
steps.feedback: A generic green claim on a mass-consumption event invites greenwashing complaints. Be precise or say nothing.

exercises.explain: In France, check reference prices, legal mentions and claims before any big campaign: the DGCCRF watches Black Friday every year.
